page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-176 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 176 dedicated vCPUs derived from 88 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 352.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The processor features an L3 cache of 105 MB and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core processing capabilities, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 146478.58 and a PassMark CPU score of 105096.7. Memory subsystem performance is also in the top decile, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 458.9 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 190.34 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1731.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1623.38. The server excels in highly parallelized tasks, achieving 164.37 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 126.23 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the c3-highcpu-176 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core, which limits its suitability for memory-bound applications despite its massive compute capacity. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage options. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high compute density and strong parallel execution capabilities per resource unit, making it highly effective for CPU-intensive workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference prompt processing.
